title: tensorfold-native capabilities --json
description: One JSON object on stdout and exit status 0, within two seconds, with no model loaded and no GPU memory allocated. `tensorfold serve` with engine auto execs the native engine only when this document lists every serve flag and value the user gave and every TENSORFOLD_ and TF_ variable that is set, and a gate entry names the checkpoint's family and weight format, the backend, this chip and this bundle. The exec passes argv ["tensorfold", "serve", the user's arguments without --engine], full flag names only, and the environment unchanged. From there the native engine behaves as the Python engine does: the same flags and defaults; the same stdout and stderr lines, flushed per line even into a pipe; `tensorfold: MESSAGE` and status 1 for a startup error, status 2 for a usage error; a graceful stop and status 0 on SIGTERM or SIGINT; the same HTTP API, /health and /metrics included; the Hugging Face cache and offline variables honoured.

schema.description: This document's format. The Python CLI keeps its own engine for any other value.

version.description: The TensorFold release the binary was built from.

chip.description: The chip class the binary would serve on here, exactly as gate entries name it: apple-m<generation> on a Mac, sm_<compute capability> on an NVIDIA GPU (sm_121 for GB10); null without a usable GPU.

families.description: Checkpoints it serves: config.json model_type to the weight formats it reads, named as gate entries name them.

flags.description: Every `tensorfold serve` flag it takes, with the Python CLI's syntax, default and meaning. A flag's values, when listed, are the only values it accepts, exactly as typed.

env.description: The TENSORFOLD_ and TF_ variables it honours as the Python engine does. HF_HOME, HF_HUB_CACHE, HF_HUB_OFFLINE, HF_TOKEN and HF_ENDPOINT are always honoured and may be listed too.
